title: Selection getting worse? Read the pattern of misroutes
head: What you observe
Where the fault is
Fix
rows: Misroutes spread evenly, started as tool count grew
Too many tools on one agent
Rare tool called when it shouldn't be
Hook to block it, if it must stay
One subagent often needs one outside capability
rule: Too many tools on one agent degrades selection. Keep the frequent tools on the front-line agent and give rare ones to a specialist.

title: Subagent needs outside help mid-task: who should supply it?
head: Situation
Right mechanism
Why
rows: Narrow cross-role tool for the subagent
Removes round trips without broad access

No tool or round trip needed

Next step depends on other subagents' findings
Subagent holds tools outside its role
rule: Scope tools to the role, then add one narrow exception for the high-frequency simple need. Complex cases stay with the coordinator.

title: What exactly must be guaranteed about tool calls?
head: What you observe
Where the fault is
Fix
rows: A specific tool must run before any text
Force that tool by name, then back to auto
Some tool call instead of plain text
Certain tools only after a prerequisite has returned
Instruction to call a tool first
Fine as guidance, not as a guarantee
rule: "any" guarantees a tool call, not which one. To make one tool run first, force it by name on that request.

title: A subagent keeps reaching outside its role: what kind of reach?
head: What you observe
Where the fault is
Fix
rows: Scoped tool such as verify_fact; complex cases via coordinator
Remove them from the AgentDefinition; report gaps
Too many tools, picks the wrong one
Cut to the 4–5 tools the role needs
Claim-source mapping, if retrieval is in role
rule: Off-role tools get used. Remove them and route real gaps back through the coordinator; keep scoped cross-role tools for frequent, simple needs.

title: Controlling a risky tool: remove, gate or guide?
head: What you observe
Where the fault is
Fix
rows: Action not allowed from the agent at all
Deny or remove the tool; keep the rest
PreToolUse hook that asks or blocks
Action allowed under a threshold, e.g. an amount
Hook blocks above it and redirects
Agent misuses tools outside its role
rule: Not allowed from the agent: remove the tool. Allowed with approval: a hook. A preference: an instruction.

title: A tool must run first: which lever controls order?
head: Need
Mechanism
Strength
rows: A specific tool first, every time
Block a call until a prerequisite is met
rule: Forced tool_choice makes a specific tool run first; "any" only guarantees some tool. Descriptions improve picking but can't promise order.

head: Situation
tool_choice
Why
rows: Must call a tool; several valid, Claude chooses well
Must call one specific tool (e.g. first step)
Tool optional; text answers are fine
rule: Need a tool call but Claude should pick which: tool_choice "any". Need one exact tool: force it by name.

title: Claude's tool calls are off: which tool_choice fixes it?
head: What you observe
Where the fault is
Fix
rows: A specific tool must run first but sometimes doesn't
Forced tool_choice naming that tool on the first request
Claude replies in text when a tool call is needed
Claude confuses two similar tools at random
Expand descriptions with inputs and boundaries
rule: any forces some tool call; a named tool_choice forces that exact tool. Use the named form to make a step run first.

title: A subagent misuses tools: description or distribution?
head: What you observe
Where the fault is
Fix
rows: Many off-role tools; descriptions already good
Scope the AgentDefinition's tool list to the role
Few tools, one-line descriptions, confused picks
Needs one quick lookup from another role, often
Many exploratory calls to learn what exists
rule: Descriptions fix confused picks among the right tools; scoping fixes holding the wrong tools.

title: Which tool_choice fits the output you need?
head: What you need
Setting
Why

rule: Several valid tools, no text allowed: any. One required tool: force it by name.
